newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SINGAPORE RUBBER QUIET, TRADE DIGEST THAI REPORTS.
newsitem.headline: SINGAPORE RUBBER QUIET, TRADE DIGEST THAI REPORTS.

text.p: Trading in the Singapore rubber market was quiet by midday on Monday with the trade digesting reports that the Thai government has denied it plans to sell an estimated 74,000 tonnes of rubber stocks, dealers said.

"The major consumers are not interested in the market at the moment. They feel prices should come down some more. They'll probably wait for leads in the afternoon and then decide on their next move," a dealer said.
Another dealer said the trade was digesting reports the Thai government had denied it planned to sell its roughly 70,000 tonnes in rubber stocks.
"The trade has almost digested it, but some are still nervous about the possibility the Thai government may just do it," one dealer said.
Most of the trade want to see if major consumers like to see if Bridgestone, Goodyear and Michelin will come into the market.
"We're waiting to hear from them, especially Michelin and Bridgestone," a trader said.
At around 0445 GMT, September RSS3 was indicated at 92.50-94.50 U.S. cents a kg from 94.50 cents.
